title: Powering AI at Scale: Optimizing Hyperscale Data Centre Infrastructure in MENA | World Economic Forum
gist: WEF summary of a MENA report warning hyperscale data-centre growth risks outpacing power, cooling and water systems, offering a resource-intelligence matrix framework; the page is an abstract only.

insights.claim: MENA governments and sovereign wealth funds are investing heavily to become a global AI hub, but electricity demand is already rising faster than supply, with extreme heat raising cooling needs and water scarcity increasing reliance on energy-intensive desalination.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Power and water, not capital, are the binding constraints on Gulf AI build-outs.

insights.claim: Hyperscale AI data centres create sustained and sometimes volatile high-density power demand that conventional grids were not built to handle, so expansion may outpace the energy and water systems that sustain it.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Grid and cooling providers and on-site generation are beneficiaries; project delay risk rises.
insights.locator: Energy infrastructure is already under strain

insights.claim: The report proposes a resource-intelligence matrix to align energy supply with AI-enabled demand management, with actions on energy optimisation, cooling and regulatory reform.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Policy direction: demand management and cooling efficiency mandates.
insights.locator: Powering AI at Scale report description
